title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Future of Apache Iceberg
gist: At QCon San Francisco, Iceberg co-creator Daniel Weeks (Databricks) presented Apache Iceberg V4 as a major, non-backward-compatible reimagining of the table format: an Adaptive Metadata Tree and single-file commits enabling second or subsecond commits, typed column statistics, constraints, and file and vector types aimed at AI and search workloads.

insights.claim: Apache Iceberg V4 is pitched by co-creator Daniel Weeks of Databricks as a major reimagining of the table format to fix V3-and-prior design flaws that surface at very large scale, rather than an incremental release.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Signals Iceberg's continued evolution as the default open lakehouse format, with Databricks deeply involved in its roadmap.
insights.quote: We didn't get everything right in V3 and prior
insights.locator: V4 is a major reimagining of a table format.

insights.claim: In Iceberg V3 adding a data file requires at least four I/O operations including manifest creation and rewriting, while V4 lets the metadata tree root point directly to data files, reducing a commit to a single metadata write.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Lower commit overhead reduces object-storage I/O cost and enables streaming use cases on lakehouse tables.
insights.locator: In V3, adding a data file requires

insights.claim: Iceberg V4's faster commits could allow commits every second or subsecond, versus the current recommendation of no commits more frequent than every two minutes.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Moves Iceberg into streaming territory, competing more directly with streaming-oriented formats like Apache Paimon and with real-time databases.
insights.quote: We can do commits at the 2nd level or subsecond level, where right now we largely recommend that you don't do commits under 2 minutes.

insights.claim: Iceberg V4 replaces V3's binary column statistics with structured typed statistics and adds relative file paths and column-level updates, improving projection and schema evolution.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Better statistics improve query planning across engines, a performance lever for engine vendors on Iceberg.
insights.locator: V4 replaces V3's binary column statistics

themes.theme: New features and AI data types

insights.claim: Iceberg V4 adds expression-based default values, check, unique and primary key constraints with tracked validation status, and statistics-only fields for partitioning, sorting and filtering without storing extra data.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Constraints bring warehouse-like semantics to open tables, narrowing the gap with proprietary warehouses.
insights.locator: Furthermore, V4 introduces expression-based default values

insights.claim: Iceberg V4 introduces file and vector data types to support AI and search workloads directly in the open table format.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Native vector support in lakehouse tables could pressure standalone vector databases for some workloads.
insights.locator: new data types, particularly file and vector types

insights.claim: Iceberg V4 metadata will not be backward compatible with older readers; V3 metadata can remain during upgrade but older readers cannot consume the new representation.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Forces coordinated engine upgrades across the ecosystem; vendors that ship V4 support first gain an edge.
insights.locator: During the Q&A, Weeks explicitly confirmed

insights.claim: Apache Iceberg competes with Delta Lake (Databricks-created, now Linux Foundation), Apache Hudi (from Uber) and Apache Paimon (from the Flink community, streaming-oriented), though interoperability tools are increasingly blurring the lines between open table formats.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Format wars are converging on interoperability, shifting competition to engines and catalogs.
insights.locator: Apache Iceberg is an open table format
